one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event in the window: Q3 2026 results, expected around 2026-10-20/21 (source 34). Q3 revenue is already pre-announced at more than 30% sequential growth, i.e. above ~$186M (sources 9-11), so the headline is mostly known. The stock will move on (a) how much of the Q3 royalty jump is a one-time catch-up versus a recurring per-module royalty from the Sep-16 VPD licensee, (b) Q4 guidance and backlog/book-to-bill after the $380M June backlog, (c) product gross margin, which has been stuck near 47-48% (sources 1, 30, 31), and (d) second-fab capex and Gen-2 VPD timing. Hyperscaler Q3 capex calls in late October also fall in the window (source 27). The stock has risen ~65% in three weeks (from $184 on 2026-09-16 to $305.61, source 26), so short-term reversal risk is real, and a disclosure that a large part of the Q3 royalty was catch-up could take back part of the move. I centre the 1-month distribution slightly below spot (median ~$300) with monthly vol ~31%, which is the stock's usual 27% (95%/3.5) scaled up for the earnings event.

fair_value.method: Blend of an SOTP-style forward P/E (60%) and a DCF (40%). P/E: recurring product EPS ~$4.07 x 38x plus recurring royalty EPS ~$2.58 x 25x on the NTM basis expected at Oct-2027 = $219. DCF (WACC 11%, g 4%, revenue to $2.25B by 2032 at a 37% EBIT margin) = $158 one year forward. Blended ~$195. One-off patent/licensing income (the $45M 2025 settlement, the $15M Q2-26 termination-clause catch-up, the estimated catch-up part of the Q3-26 VPD royalty) and one-off tax benefits are excluded.

methods.name: P/E

$60M base licensees + $30M Q2-26 licence (5+5+10+10) + $50M VPD; 2028 grows with AI module volumes and the four OEM/hyperscaler licensees (source 10)

2026E product = H1 $211M + Q3 ~$138M + Q4 ~$155M, consistent with the $643M 2026 consensus incl. royalties. 2027 growth is backed by the $380M one-year backlog, Fab 1 capacity of $1B-$1.5B run-rate, and base-case 2027 AI capex of $1.84T ex-China (+50%).
Product GM = total GM less royalties (assumed ~100% margin): Q4-25 48.4%, Q1-26 48.4%, Q2-26 46.7%, the last hurt by one-time equipment relocation. Management expects expansion as Fab 1 fills.

Inside the peer range of 21.9-64.6x and above the 29.2x median, between MPWR (46x) and VRT/POWI (32x). Vicor's product growth (~35-40%) is similar to peers', not structurally higher. Its margins are below MPWR's and customer concentration is high, so it gets no premium above the upper half of the range.
Below the peer median. The stream is ~100% margin but depends on ITC enforcement (second ITC case final determination in 2027), finite patent life and contracts that are renegotiated every two years.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue 2027-2032: $840M, $1,130M, $1,420M, $1,720M, $2,000M, $2,250M; EBIT margin 33% -> 37%; tax 20%; capex $200M/$220M in 2027-28 (second fab) then $120-160M; WACC 11%; terminal growth 4%; net cash $446M; 48.5M shares; rolled forward 1 year at 11%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's long-term target is $2.5B and needs the second fab, which ramps in late 2027-2028. I reach ~90% of the target by 2032 to haircut execution risk.
No cost was disclosed. Sized from the current capex run-rate (~$12M/qtr) and a fab with 2-3x Fab 1's capacity, built in phases.
High equity risk: 95% realised vol, customer concentration and litigation-dependent royalties. No debt.

bear.story: Q3 royalty turns out to be mostly catch-up and the recurring VPD royalty is small. Gen-2 VPD slips beyond late 2027, product GM stays near 48%, and an AI capex digestion (2027 low case $1.39T) slows orders. About $4.5 NTM EPS x ~31x (peer median) = ~$140, roughly where the stock was before the licensing news (sources 26, 27).

base.story: Product revenue grows ~40% in 2027 as Fab 1 fills, royalties settle near $35M/qtr, and the second fab is funded from cash. NTM EPS at Oct-27 ~$6.6, valued at ~39x: a premium to the peer median that the market keeps paying for the AI licensing optionality, but below today's 56x.

bull.story: More hyperscalers license VPD, helped by ITC exclusion pressure. Royalties run above $300M/yr, Gen-2 VPD wins sockets on Rubin-generation and ASIC platforms, and the $2.5B path becomes credible. ~$8.7 NTM EPS x 55x, in line with the stock's current multiple and ALAB.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 21.9x (AEIS) to 64.6x (ALAB); forward EV/EBITDA 6.6x (ON) to 78.2x (ALAB). P/E is StockAnalysis 'forward PE' (NTM consensus) for every peer, priced at the 2026-10-05 close. Forward EV/EBITDA is my estimate: TTM EV/EBITDA x (forward P/E / trailing P/E), which assumes EBITDA grows in line with EPS. It is distorted where GAAP trailing earnings are depressed (ON, POWI).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: VICR trades at 56.3x NTM consensus EPS (~$5.43) and ~119x TTM EV/EBITDA, against a 29.2x peer median and only ALAB higher. My fair value uses 38x for recurring product earnings (upper half of the range) and 25x for recurring royalties (below the median). Blended this is ~33x NTM-at-horizon EPS, above the median and inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The modest premium to the median rests on two things that should persist through the horizon. First, the royalty stream is nearly 100% margin and contractual, from four OEM/hyperscaler licensees, which lifts consolidated returns on capital. Second, Vicor carries $446M of net cash and no debt. Against that, product gross margin (~47%) is well below MPWR's, customers are highly concentrated (10-K: the majority of Advanced Products revenue comes from one or a few customers), and royalties depend on ITC enforcement. So I do not go to MPWR or ALAB multiples. Sell-side targets ($320-450) are not used as justification.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 the stock would have given back the entire VPD-licensing move ($184 on 2026-09-16) and more. At that level the market would most likely be pricing a fundamental failure, not normal 95%-vol noise: the VPD royalty proving mostly one-off or a licence lost or invalidated (e.g. an adverse ITC or appeal outcome), Gen-2 VPD failing to win 2027 sockets, or a sustained AI capex cut showing up as backlog shrinkage below ~$250M.

reasoning: Primary documents give a cleaner earnings base than the headlines. Reported H1-26 EPS of $1.48 and FY25 EPS of $2.61 are inflated by one-offs: the $45M Q2-25 patent settlement, the $15M Q2-26 termination-clause catch-up on a new licence, a -27.9% Q2-26 tax rate from option exercises and a $27.3M Q4-25 DTA release (sources 1, 5, 30, 31). Recurring royalties ran ~$15M/qtr before the new deals. Product revenue is growing fast (+32% y/y in Q2; backlog $380M, +145% y/y), but product gross margin is only ~47-48%. In September Vicor signed its first non-exclusive VPD licence and raised Q3 guidance twice, to >30% sequential, i.e. revenue above ~$186M (sources 8-11). The stock rose from $184 to $306. Building 2027-28 from recurring parts gives NTM-at-horizon EPS of ~$6.65. On peer-bounded multiples (11 peers, NTM P/E median 29x, range 22-65x) plus a DCF, fair value is ~$195. That is below spot because today's 56x NTM is near the top of the peer range and I cannot argue a persistent premium of that size. The AI capex base case (2027 +50% to $1.84T ex-China) supports the product growth assumptions but is already in consensus. For the distribution I do not put the median at the fundamental value: names like this can hold AI multiples for a year, the licensing optionality is real (four licensees, ITC leverage), and sell-side targets average $386. I put the 12-month median at ~$265, between fair value and spot, with lognormal-like dispersion of ~75% (below the 95% realised vol, which was inflated by the 2026 re-rating), a fat right tail for the bull case, and scenario weights 30/45/25 (expected value ~$280). Research was limited to filings, company releases and transcripts plus data pages. Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data fundamentals were unavailable (rate limit or plan). Because the peer-comp requirement needed one data page per peer (11 of 34 sources), in-lane sources come to 13 of 34. Excluding the peer-data pages, 13 of 23 are in-lane. No option prices or implied volatility were used.
